card.name: Verbs of drug action and impaired response
card.fires_on: The word right after a drug or drug class that describes how it acts or how well it works, such as "acts", "act", "acting" or "impaired response". It also fires on a few nearby slots, such as "partial or complete" before loss of vision.

modes.label: Acts on a site
modes.description: Forms of "act" after a drug name or class, describing where or how it works.
modes.example: a second diuretic that<< acts>> more proximally in the renal tub

modes.label: Impaired response
modes.description: The word "response" after "impaired" in warnings about reduced effect of diuretics or blood pressure drugs.
modes.example: loop diuretics may have impaired<< response>> to these therapies when taking NSAIDs.

card.writes: It seems to push toward word choices in a "capacity or effect" sense, and away from "ability" and "capability" words.
card.plain: It marks the spot where a label says how a drug acts or how well the body responds to it.
